tier_reason: The benchmark_url SVG is a thread-scaling plot whose every curve starts at exactly 1.0 at one thread, so it is giotto-ph against its own single-thread run, not against Ripser; the Ripser v1.2 comparison and the Ripser++ claim are first-party (arXiv 2107.05412 via search snippet, v0.1.0 release notes) with no reachable numbers, CPU, compiler, flags or benchmark code. First-party claim without methodology stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README figure (multithreading_speedup.svg) is self-relative thread scaling, normalized to 1.0 at one thread for every dataset (derived from page data by reading the SVG path coordinates): at 48 threads fractal about 23.7x, o3_4096 about 14.2x, random16 about 12.9x, o3_1024 about 10.2x, torus4 about 10.1x, sphere3 about 1.7x, dragon about 1.06x (dragon peaks about 1.5x between 5 and 11 threads). Against Ripser v1.2 the paper (arXiv 2107.05412, search snippet only) says giotto-ph performs very similarly on one thread and is faster whenever more than one thread is used; v0.1.0 release notes say it surpasses 'GPU-accelerated implementations such as Ripser++ when using as few as 5-10 CPU cores'. No head-to-head times against Ripser or Ripser++ were reachable.
corrections.caveats: The README figure is giotto-ph's own thread scaling (every curve is 1.0 at one thread), not a head-to-head with Ripser; the speedup over Ripser v1.2 can only be inferred by combining it with the paper's statement (search snippet only, arXiv blocked) that single-thread giotto-ph performs about like Ripser v1.2. The paper's Figure 2 (giotto-ph vs Ripser v1.2) and its Ripser++ comparison could not be opened. No CPU model, core count (axis reaches 48 threads), compiler or flags appear in the README, release notes or repo, and the repo has no benchmark folder or benchmark code. Gains are small on easy datasets (sphere3 about 1.7x, dragon about 1.06x at 48 threads). Licensed AGPL-3.0 (copyleft), and the last commit (2024-05-30) is over two years old. Ripserer.jl issue #168 (the lead) has no speed data.

notes: Shortcoming: benchmark figure is self-relative thread scaling, not a Ripser head-to-head; Ripser and Ripser++ wins are first-party paper/release-note claims seen only via snippet, no hardware, compiler, flags or benchmark code. Metadata checked: 59 stars, AGPL-3.0 per README and LICENSE file, last commit 2024-05-30 (stale), not archived or a fork.

tier_reason: The morton-nd README numbers (GCC 11.1.0, -O3 -DNDEBUG, i9-9980HK, harness in the kevinhartman/libmorton fork, whose README says its CMakeLists.txt adds -mbmi2) are reproducible, but they only compare libmorton's BMI2 path with libmorton's own LUT paths and with morton-nd (parity), never with an external incumbent or the loop and magic-bits baselines, whose numbers sit in unreachable forceflow.be posts; an intra-library comparison stays at C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 11.1.0 on macOS 11.1 with -O3 -DNDEBUG (morton-nd README); the kevinhartman/libmorton fork README states its CMakeLists.txt sets -mbmi2 to enable the BMI2 test paths (the CMakeLists.txt itself was not found at the fork's root)
corrections.caveats: The repo README contains no numbers; it points to three forceflow.be blog posts (2013 bit-interleaving, 2016 libmorton, 2016 BMI2) that hold the real benchmarks, and that host does not resolve here. The only numbers found are third-party (morton-nd README) and compare libmorton's BMI2 path with libmorton's own LUT paths, so no external incumbent and none of the loop or magic-bits baselines is measured. The same table shows morton-nd's generated code at parity with or slightly ahead of libmorton (32-bit 3D encode: morton-nd 1-chunk 10-bit LUT 524.178 ms linear vs libmorton BMI2 530.421 ms). The 'definitely a faster method' line is libmorton's own README prose about BMI2, without numbers. PR #40 (AVX512 vs BMI2 on an i7-1065G7, compiler not stated) shows the experimental AVX512 path roughly equal to BMI2.

notes: Shortcoming: only intra-library BMI2-vs-LUT numbers (1.14x to 1.84x, derived) from a third-party README, no external incumbent or loop/magic-bits baseline measured; blog benchmarks unreachable. All claimed_speedup numbers match the morton-nd README rows; metadata checked (667 stars, MIT, last commit 2026-06-16, active).
